EXPLANATION.TITLE: FAQ on the tenant concept and access protection for datasets
EXPLANATION.DESCRIPTION: Overview and usage notes for the access control introduced with KomMonitor version 4

TENANT.TITLE: What is a tenant?
TENANT.CONTENT:
KomMonitor allows the creation of different groups in order to model administrative structures and to assign access rights in a dedicated way.
A KomMonitor group can be marked as a tenant by the KomMonitor super administrator. Like a root node in a hierarchy tree, this tenant serves to model further subgroups.

Within a KomMonitor instance, several tenants can be created independently of each other, each managing its own, separate subgroup hierarchies, spatial levels and datasets.

CREATE_TENANT.TITLE: How are new tenants created?
CREATE_TENANT.CONTENT:
1. Log in as a user with KomMonitor super administrator rights (role kommonitor-creator)
  2. Navigate to the group management menu and click the Create button
  3. When creating the new group, set the checkmark for the tenant property
  4. Provide the remaining metadata and create the group.
  5. So that the new group may manage itself (and, if applicable, subgroups), it must still be given the corresponding rights. To do so, click the Edit group-specific rights button in the overview table of the group management. In the corresponding menu, in step 2 - Rights of others, set at least the rights for managing users, resources and topics for this group.

    Setting a Subgroups checkmark causes this group to also co-administer all of its subgroups with respect to users, topics or resources.
  6. Create the tenant administrator user in Keycloak and assign them to the Keycloak group of the same name.

From this point on, the new tenant is operational. Tenant administrators have the rights to create further subgroups, users and datasets within a tenant.

SUBGROUPS.TITLE: What are subgroups of a tenant?
SUBGROUPS.CONTENT:
Within a tenant, any number of subgroups can optionally be created. While a tenant group alone is already sufficient to fully manage datasets in KomMonitor, creating further subgroup hierarchies allows a fine-grained division of responsibilities and more targeted dataset sharing within the administration.

A subgroup can also be co-administered by parent groups with respect to users, resources and topics - depending on the rights that have been set.

CREATE_SUBGROUPS.TITLE: How are new subgroups created?
CREATE_SUBGROUPS.CONTENT:
1. Log in as a member user of a parent group with user management rights
  2. Navigate to the group management menu and click the Create button
  3. When creating the new subgroup, select the corresponding parent group
  4. Provide the remaining metadata and create the subgroup.
  5. optional: In the submenu 2 - Rights of others, specify whether already existing other groups should take over administrative tasks for the new subgroup.

    If the parent group may co-manage all of its subgroups, this does not have to be set explicitly again here.
  6. optional: If the subgroup should also take over selected administrative tasks for itself (and, if applicable, further subgroups), it must still be given the corresponding rights. To do so, click the Edit group-specific rights button in the overview table of the group management. In the corresponding menu, in step 2 - Rights of others, set all relevant rights for managing users, resources or topics for this group.

    Setting a Subgroups checkmark causes this group to also co-administer all of its subgroups with respect to users, topics or resources.
  7. Create or find the corresponding users in Keycloak and assign them to the Keycloak subgroup of the same name.

OWNERSHIP.TITLE: What is the ownership of datasets?
OWNERSHIP.CONTENT:
When creating new spatial units, indicators and georesources, it is required to specify which group owns the resource.

A resource can only belong to exactly one group. Only members of the owner group of a resource have the right to control the data sharing of the dataset and to delete a resource.

CHANGE_OWNERSHIP.TITLE: Can the ownership be changed?
CHANGE_OWNERSHIP.CONTENT:
Yes, super administrators with the role kommonitor-creator as well as members of the owner group can transfer the ownership to another existing group.
  1. Log in as a member user of the owner group
  2. Navigate to the resource management (spatial units, indicators or georesources) and click the Edit access protection and ownership button
  3. In the submenu 3 - Ownership, select the new group and irrevocably cede the ownership via the Update button.

GROUP_SHARING.TITLE: How does the group-specific sharing of a dataset work?
GROUP_SHARING.CONTENT:
Members of the owner group of a dataset (spatial unit, indicator or georesource) always have full access to the resource (read, edit, delete).

Already when creating a resource, members of the owner group specify in the Access protection and ownership step which other groups are granted read and edit rights. In a tabular form, the corresponding checkmarks are set in the applicable group rows.

A subsequent change is possible at any time in the respective resource management menu via the Access protection and ownership button and its submenus. Adjustments only take effect when the Update button is pressed.

PUBLIC_SHARING.TITLE: How does the public sharing of datasets work?
PUBLIC_SHARING.CONTENT:
Similar to the group-specific sharing of datasets, only members of the owner group of a dataset (spatial unit, indicator or georesource) are permitted to set up public read access to the resource.

Already when creating a resource, members of the owner group explicitly specify in the Access protection and ownership step, via the Public read access switch, whether the dataset may also be retrieved without a user login.

A subsequent change is possible at any time in the respective resource management menu via the Access protection and ownership button and its submenus. Adjustments only take effect when the Update button is pressed.

INDICATOR_SHARING.TITLE: How does the data sharing of indicators for specific spatial units work?
INDICATOR_SHARING.CONTENT:
Special rules apply to the sharing (read, edit) of indicators. In principle, KomMonitor distinguishes for indicators between the sharing of their metadata and the sharing of concrete time series on concrete linked spatial units. For example, it is configurable to publicly share the indicator with respect to its metadata as well as the time series of selected spatial units, while time series of very small-scale spatial units should only be available to the internal administration.

Furthermore, in addition to sharing the indicators, a precisely matching sharing of the spatial units must also be set. In the following, some example scenarios are distinguished and illustrated with configuration hints:

SCENARIO_PRIVATE.TITLE: Scenario: indicator not public
SCENARIO_PRIVATE.CONTENT:
Indicator metadataIndicator time series per spatial levelSpatial unit metadata
Deactivate the Public read access switchper spatial unit:
explicit sharing with relevant groups (read, write) different configurations per spatial unit are conceivable		Read access to the spatial unit metadata itself must be granted analogously to all relevant groups.

SCENARIO_PARTIAL.TITLE: Scenario: indicator partially public
SCENARIO_PARTIAL.CONTENT:
Indicator metadataIndicator time series per spatial levelSpatial unit metadata
Activate the Public read access switchper spatial unit:
  • for all spatial units with public access, activate the Public read access (further explicit sharing with groups only if needed for edit rights)
  • for internal spatial units, deactivate the Public read access – instead, only explicit sharing with relevant groups (read, write)
different configurations per spatial unit are conceivable		Activate public read access for certain spatial unit metadata.
Internal protected read access to other spatial unit metadata must be granted explicitly to all relevant groups analogously.

SCENARIO_PUBLIC.TITLE: Scenario: indicator completely public
SCENARIO_PUBLIC.CONTENT:
Indicator metadataIndicator time series per spatial levelSpatial unit metadata
Activate the Public read access switchfor all spatial units, activate the Public read access (further explicit sharing with groups only if needed for edit rights) different configurations per spatial unit are conceivableactivate public read access on the affected spatial unit metadata itself

INTRO.OVERVIEW: KomMonitor allows the automated continuation/computation of indicators from georesources or other (sub-)indicators. Two steps are required:
INTRO.FIRST_STEP: First step: Selection / creation of the target indicator to be computed via the indicator management. The following points must be taken into account:
INTRO.CHECK_CONTINUATION_TYPE: The continuation type of the target indicator is set to "automatic computation by KomMonitor".
INTRO.CHECK_UPDATE_INTERVAL: The update interval of the target indicator is not set to "arbitrary".
INTRO.CHECK_MISSING_TIMESTAMPS: The script computation is only performed for missing timestamps. To trigger a recomputation, an entire timestamp of the target indicator can be removed via the indicator deletion menu.
INTRO.CHECK_NO_EDITING: Editing the script configuration for computing the target indicator afterwards is currently not possible. Instead, an existing script must be removed and created anew.
INTRO.SECOND_STEP: Second step: Creation of the computation script via the script management, selecting the previously defined target indicator.
INTRO.SCHEDULER_INFO: The overall KomMonitor system includes a so-called Processing Scheduler, which automatically triggers the computation of the target indicator timestamps based on the script and indicator metadata. The computation itself is performed by the Processing Engine component.
INTRO.ACCESS_RIGHTS_WARNING: If new spatial units are linked to indicators for the first time by the computation script, the access rights are taken over from the associated metadata.
